system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Trapezoid ABCD with diagonals intersecting to form four numbered triangles]
AB is parallel to DC

Two of the four triangles in the figure above are the same shape but different sizes. Shade in those two triangles.

Figure, described in words:
A trapezoid labeled ABCD, with horizontal base AB at the bottom and a shorter horizontal side DC at the top. The non-parallel sides are AD on the left and BC on the right. Diagonals AC and BD intersect inside the trapezoid, dividing it into four triangles numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4: triangle 1 is at the top with base DC; triangle 2 is on the right with side BC; triangle 3 is at the bottom with base AB; and triangle 4 is on the left with side AD. Below segment AB is the text "AB is parallel to DC".

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Shade triangle 1 (the top triangle with base DC) and triangle 3 (the bottom triangle with base AB). Because AB is parallel to DC, these two triangles have equal corresponding angles and are similar, so they have the same shape but different sizes. Triangles 2 and 4 are not the same shape as each other or as triangles 1 and 3, so they should not be shaded.

llm_thinking: The diagonals of the trapezoid split it into four triangles meeting at O - top (DOC), bottom (AOB), left (AOD), and right (BOC). Since DC is parallel to AB, triangles DOC and AOB are similar to each other, so those are the two to shade.
